feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no result is stated for it. What I had to do in the controller: nothing beyond keeping the iteration 7 gains (kp 0.8, kd 0.15, ki 0, base_speed 1.5). The Builder's test changes only mass, so I held the controller fixed to keep the result comparable with 73.33. Evidence: mass 0.6 kg gave 55.45, 0.8 kg gave 69.18 and 1.0 kg gave 73.33, all with the 80 mm row and 0.12 m track, so the trend is up but flattening. Oval progress rose from 0.148 (0.6 kg) to 0.229 (0.8 kg) and 0.227 (1.0 kg), so progress has plateaued. Max error stayed at 0.060 to 0.067 m on every track in every run, so the peak is still a bend transient. Decision rules for the next race: if 1.2 kg scores above 73.33 with max_error falling, the optimum is above 1.0 kg, so keep 1.2 kg and test wheel_radius next. If 1.2 kg scores below 73.33 while oval progress holds, 1.0 kg is near the local optimum, so return to 1.0 kg and test wheel_radius. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.18 on the s-bend or slalom, the heavier robot is under-damped, so the next step is a kd change in the controller (for example 0.18), not a geometry change.
requested_changes: Try wheel_radius 0.035 m with everything else at the best mass found (1.2 kg if it beats 73.33, otherwise 1.0 kg). Iterations 3 to 7 reached only 0.12 to 0.23 of the course, far short of the full run needed to finish in 3 s; a larger wheel gives more ground speed at the same PWM (hypothesis from the progress shortfall, not yet measured).

If the slalom still shows 2.0 line-loss events (iterations 0, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7) with max_error above 0.06 m, try sensor_size 0.016 m on the 80 mm row as a single test. A larger footprint keeps readings above the 0.05 line-loss threshold for longer. Iteration 1 changed sensor size together with other variables, so this effect is not yet proven.

If 1.2 kg raises s-bend steering_oscillation above about 0.18, keep the geometry and request a single kd change to 0.18 in the controller, since iteration 7 showed the mass trend still rising but the bend response may now be under-damped.
